parole.significato: A Breton band composed of bagpipes, bombards, and drums.
A set of traditional Breton bagpipes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Breton binioù, plural of béni.

parole.significato: a traditional folk song from Brittany
A lamprophyre mineral containing biotite and plagioclase.
parole.testo: From Breton, after the village of Kersanton, Brittany, France, where the rock was first identified.

parole.significato: A traditional Breton dish of various meats simmered in a broth with a buckwheat-flour pudding.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Breton kig ha farz (literally “meat and stuffing”).
From Breton korr and Cornish korr.

parole.significato: A long-haired nocturnal and often malevolent mythological creature of Breton and Welsh tradition.
parole.testo: From Breton korred, properly plural of korr; see also Welsh corrod, plural of cor. Cognate with Cornish korr.

parole.significato: A long-haired nocturnal and often malevolent Breton fairy princess; such creatures considered collectively.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Breton korrigan, from korr (“dwarf”) + -ig (diminutive suffix) + -an (hypocoristic suffix).

parole.significato: A traditional Breton cake made of layers of butter, dough, and sugar.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Breton kouign-amann, from kouign (“brioche; bun; cake”) (ultimately from Latin cuneus (“wedge”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”)) + amann (“butter”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₃engʷ- (“to anoint; to smear”)).
